result.topic_en: Power series expansions of the arcsine of the lemniscate (inverse function), of the lemniscatic sine sin x, of the lemniscatic cosine cos x, and of the auxiliary functions P, Q, p, q, with remarks on their convergence.

methods.what: Power series of the lemniscatic arcsine (integral of 1/sqrt(1-x^4))
Power series of the lemniscatic sine
Power series of auxiliary function P (numerator of lemniscatic sine), also with factorial denominators
Power series of auxiliary function Q (denominator function), with factorial denominators
Power series of the lemniscatic cosine
Common power series for auxiliary functions p and q (differing in sign of alternate terms)
Convergence statement: P,Q,p,q series entire; sin series diverges for x>pi/sqrt2, cos series for x>pi
methods.quote:
formulae
autem pro $\sin x$, [-$\cos x$-] divergent si $x$ ponatur $>$
$\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}}$ sive $x^4 > \frac{\pi^4}{4}$; formula autem pro $\cos x$ diverget
si $x > \pi$

items.quote:
Formulae pro $P, Q, p, q. x$ in infinitum continuatae
quavis convergentia data citius convergunt
items.english: The formulae for P, Q, p, q of x, continued to infinity, converge faster than any given convergence.

items.quote:
formulae
autem pro $\sin x$, [-$\cos x$-] divergent si $x$ ponatur $>$
$\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}}$ sive $x^4 > \frac{\pi^4}{4}$; formula autem pro $\cos x$ diverget
si $x > \pi$
items.english: But the formulae for sin x diverge if x is set greater than pi/sqrt2, i.e. x^4 > pi^4/4; the formula for cos x, however, will diverge if x > pi.
